Deliberate differences: only http:// endpoints without query, fragment or embedded credentials are accepted (no TLS client in the audit feature; Go also spoke HTTPS), appends after close are dropped and counted, and only 2xx is success. Re-reviewed 2026-11-18 (PR #129 review follow-up): the 10 s REQUEST_TIMEOUT is now one total deadline per insert, matching Go http.Client.Timeout: lookup, connect, request write, status and header read and the quoted error body all run through DeadlineStream against one Instant, so a trickling server can no longer hold flush past it; a missed deadline fails the insert and counts its rows as dropped. The crate-private with_request_timeout constructor lets tests shrink the deadline. The 1xx case of the 2xx-only difference is now spelled out in the module docs. Re-reviewed 2026-11-19 (FM11 residual 14): rows are now the record's Go encoding/json bytes through projection::go_json (<, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 escaped; Go float spelling such as 1, 1e-7 and 1e+21), batch_body returns the body and the encoded row count, and a record Go could not encode (NaN or infinite confidence) is left out as in Go and counted as dropped, with an all-unencodable batch not posted. The quoted error body is no longer trimmed (Go kept a trailing newline). https:// endpoints are accepted only by ClickHouseSink::with_tls (feature audit-tls, part of the default gateway set) with a caller-supplied rustls ClientConfig whose roots decide trust and the endpoint host as server name; the request and response run over rustls::StreamOwned on the same DeadlineStream, so the one total insert deadline covers the handshake. ClickHouseSink::new still refuses https:// rather than pick a root store. The module docs list every remaining difference (explicit trust roots, refused endpoint forms, append after close, 2xx only, unencodable rows counted, no User-Agent or Accept-Encoding, Connection: close). Re-reviewed 2026-11-19 (PR #139 policy follow-up): the TLS-only Target.host and Shared.tls fields are now compiled only with the audit-tls feature, so an audit-only build carries no unused fields; behavior is unchanged. Re-reviewed 2026-11-19 (PR #139 review follow-up): with_tls now refuses a plain http:// endpoint (fail-closed), so a caller that asked for TLS never sends Basic auth in clear text.

reviews.reviewer: claude agent first-pass review 2026-11-16 (Claude Code session; owner sample pending)
reviews.notes: Pure in-process Authority invariants. ALLOW comes only from a frozen synthetic fixture and only after durable audit append; the response has seven fields and the record holds no UA, body or credential. Wrong bearer gives 401, wrong peer, tenant, origin, authority, installation or admin path gives 403, and stale revision or unknown route gives 409. Replay and changed-target replay are refused, and a restart rotates the credential. Without a collector no ALLOW is fabricated, and missing required raw TLS, H2, collector or RIT signals give 422. Audit failure gives 503, plus body-hash 422, expiry 400 and capacity 429. Clock rollback cannot revive an evicted nonce, and cancellation before commit keeps the nonce spent. It is not a production security profile.

reviews.reviewer: claude agent review 2026-11-18 (Claude Code session; owner sample pending)
reviews.notes: Shipped-binary inherited witness input: inherited_witness(config) returns None when audit.witness_input is absent and refuses when witness_input_valid() is false. On Unix it reopens the configured read and write descriptors through /proc/self/fd/N (or /dev/fd/N) with O_NONBLOCK, requires both to be FIFOs, then restores blocking mode; on Linux it first checks each descriptor's access mode in /proc/self/fdinfo. It bootstraps WitnessServiceClient::from_ready either pinned to the configured trusted head and consistency proof or as new history, checks the pinned witness and writer keys, and maps the configured durability (file_and_directory, or file_synced_namespace_unconfirmed to FileSynced) into ExternalWitness.
